sentences.text: Hon'Ble Smt. Justice T. Madhavi Devi

Writ Petition No.19859 of 2020
Order:

This writ petition is filed under Article 226 of the Constitution of India seeking a Writ of Mandamus to declare the action of respondents No.2 to 4 in not implementing the G.O.Ms.No.98 Irrigation (Projects Wing) Department, dated 15.04.1986 issued by respondent No.1 by filling up only 50% of the available 350 posts with land losers, instead the respondents filling up all 350 posts with land losers, without issuing any notification and without giving any opportunity to the petitioners for consideration in any suitable posts in the respondent organization, as illegal and arbitrary and consequently, to direct the respondents to implement the said G.O.Ms.No.98, dated 15.04.1986 and to consider the petitioners in any suitable posts in the respondent organization and to pass such other order or orders, as this Court deems fit and proper.
2. The brief facts, leading to the filing of the present writ petition, are that the petitioners claim to be working as contract workers with the respondent organization for a long period.

It is submitted that as per G.O.Ms.No.98, dated 15.04.1986, the respondents are required to fill up 50% of the posts with the displaced persons or their dependants and balance posts are to be filled up by other persons.

The complaint of the petitioners is that the respondents have filled up all the 350 posts of Trainee Junior Assistants and Trainee Junior Plant Attendants with the land losers only and not by other candidates in violation of the G.O.Ms.No.98, dated 15.04.1986.
3.

The respondents have filed a counter affidavit stating that where the land was acquired by the Government after 01.01.2014, the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 (for short 'the Act') shall apply to all such Projects and in this case, since the land was acquired in the year 2016, the said Act would apply and in accordance with the provisions of said Act, the District Collector has passed an award along with the list of persons who were displaced due to the Project and the respondents have accordingly given 307 appointments in the categories of Trainee Junior Assistants, Trainee Junior Plant Attendants,
Office Sub-ordinates, House-keepers, Security guards and Firemen as per their eligibility in the month of July/September 2021.

entities.text: Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: As regards the petitioners herein are concerned, it is submitted that they have been working as contract workers.
It is submitted that there is no scheme for their absorption into the respondent organization and therefore, they cannot seek absorption as a matter of right.

4. The learned counsel for the petitioners, however, submitted that the Government has framed the Rules under the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Rules, 2014 in G.O.Ms.No.50 Revenue (JA&LA) Department, dated 19.12.2014 and there is no reference to G.O.Ms.No.98, dated 15.04.1986 thereunder and hence, G.O.Ms.No.50 is not applicable.

sentences.text: Having regard to the rival contentions and the material placed on record, this Court finds that the petitioners are contract workers and not land losers.
The only ground on which the petitioners are seeking consideration is G.O.Ms.No.98, dated 15.04.1986.
The said G.O. prescribed that only 50% of the vacancies are to be filled up by the land losers quota.

6. The learned Standing Counsel appearing for the respondents No.2 to 5 submitted that under Section 2H of the Act, there is an obligation on the part of the respondents to provide employment to the land losers identified by the District Collector and the appointments given by the respondents are not on the basis of any vacancy position in the organization pursuant to the Act.
Therefore, it is not the case where the respondents have issued a notification for direct recruitment and G.O.Ms.No.98 would be applicable.

7. It is submitted that G.O.Ms.No.98 dated 15.04.1986 was issued in order to provide employment to the displaced persons or their dependants in case of acquisition of land for Major & Medium Irrigation and Power Projects and after the enactment of the said Act, the displaced persons have been provided a right to seek employment or compensation under the Act itself and in accordance with the award passed, the respondent organization is duty bound to provide employment to all the displaced persons.
Therefore, after the enactment of said Act, G.O.Ms.No.98 dated 15.04.1986 would not have any relevancy.
Admittedly, in this case, the land was acquired in the year 2016 and the employment was provided thereafter.
The petitioners also claim that they have been working as contract workers in the organization from the year 2014 after the Act has come into force.

Therefore,
this Court does not find any merit in the writ petition.
8. Accordingly, the writ petition is dismissed.

However, the petitioners are at liberty to make a representation to the concerned authorities who shall consider the same, if there is any scheme available in the respondent organization for absorption of such employees.
No costs.
Miscellaneous applications, if any pending in this writ petition, shall stand closed.
